events.title: Jazz and Justice Festival
events.short_description: Six hours of live music on the hill, and we put the whole thing on the air.
events.full_description:
Six hours of live music on the hill, and we put the whole thing on the air. Edwin Ortiz & La Mafia Del Guaguanco open the dance floor, Blue Note trumpeter Brandon Woody follows, then Grammy-nominated MuMu Fresh, Proverbs Reggae Band, and Be'la Dona closing it out with go-go. Between the sets, the programmers you hear all week step out from behind the glass, along with an elders circle, a libation, and poets. Across 15th Street at the Josephine Butler Parks Center, community discussions run from noon until seven, documentary screenings from one, alongside yoga, meditation, an art gallery, and the vendor village.

The Sunday drum circle opens the day, as it has on this hill since 1965.

Bring a blanket and bring your people. We'll see you on the new date.

Watch for it: https://www.wpfwdc.org/jazz-and-justice-festival

events.title: WPFW 50th Anniversary Gala
events.short_description: An evening honoring five decades of community-powered radio: music, guest speakers, special tributes, and the people who have kept 89.3 on the air since 1977. Tickets on sale in November.
events.full_description:
WPFW turns fifty on February 28, 2027, and this is the night the station marks it. An evening of music, guest speakers and special tributes at Martin's Crosswinds in Greenbelt, Maryland.

Some of the people in that room signed the station on in 1977. Some found 89.3 last week on a car radio. It is the first real chance in a long time to get listeners, volunteers, programmers and staff under one roof.

Tickets go on sale in November. The start time will be announced here and on the air.
